title: G-kway: Multilevel GPU-Accelerated k-way Graph Partitioner
problem: Graph partitioning becomes increasingly time-consuming as graph sizes grow, which is critical for CAD algorithm design. Existing partitioning solutions lack sufficient performance for large-scale graphs.
motivation: Efficient graph partitioning is essential for CAD algorithms, and accelerating this process enables handling of large and complex graphs.
method: G-kway speeds up graph partitioning using a multilevel approach on a GPU. It shrinks the graph using union find (a technique that groups connected pieces together while preserving their connections), then partitions this smaller version. During uncoarsening (expanding back to the original size), it refines the partition by rearranging independent sets of nodes (groups of unconnected nodes that can move together). Running all these steps on a GPU makes the entire process much faster than using a regular processor.
key_novelty: The key technique is using union find-based coarsening and independent set-based refinement algorithms on a GPU instead of a regular processor, which makes multilevel graph partitioning much faster.
contributions: Efficient GPU-accelerated union find-based coarsening algorithm
Novel independent set-based refinement algorithm for GPU uncoarsening
Significant acceleration of both coarsening and uncoarsening stages
8.6× speedup over CPU partitioners and 3.8× over GPU baselines with comparable quality
